segments.script: Annotate the chapter for structure, dialogue (three marks with a margin note each), then write one claim-evidence-reasoning paragraph: what does this chapter suggest about the first proposal? Then start your writing prompt at your assigned level (HS Sophomore: Analyze how Chapter XXXIV develops the idea of the first proposal. Make a precise claim, support it with at least three pieces of textual evidence, and explain how the author's use of conflict and characterization shapes that idea. Address one possible counterclaim.) Exemplar: The proposal fails because Darcy's pride and Elizabeth's prejudice collide. When the text says “You could not have made me the offer of your hand in any possible way that would have tempted me to accept it” (Chapter XXXIV, paragraph 26), it shows this directly. He confesses "in vain have I struggled," dwelling on her inferiority even as he declares love, and she replies that no offer "in any possible way" could have tempted her.
